clue.text: Noble type had a celebration first

indicators.note: first tells us the celebration comes before the other word in the build

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration or event
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aristocrat threw a party before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the celebration, GALA, ahead of HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad, the purest knight of the Round Table, stands for any nobly chivalrous man.

clue.text: Look, a bird

explanation.definitionFit: A gander is slang for a look or glance, and also a male goose.

clue.text: Tactile arrangement for network

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A touch-based layout is proposed for a network.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross framework of strips, a mesh or grid.

clue.text: Botanical expert sees woman's island on the way

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting above, so the road comes underneath

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
Bali is an Indonesian island
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A plant specialist visits a woman's island while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist studies and uses plants for their medicinal properties.

clue.text: Get the bird gradually, in spreading fashion

parts.note: a diver is a diving water bird, the loon
gently can mean gradually, as in a gently sloping hill

explanation.surface: Someone is advised to approach a bird slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Divergent lines move apart, so the adverb describes things branching out.

clue.text: Encourages mad scientist? No way!

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters of scientist are crazily jumbled

parts.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A deranged researcher is egged on, with an exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of SCIENTIST, 'mad', are the answer plus ST ('way'), so 'No way!' tells you to take ST out of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to stir up or urge on, the same as to encourage.

clue.text: Local river

explanation.definitionFit: A 'local' is British for one's neighbourhood pub, a kind of tavern; the Inn is a river flowing from Switzerland through Austria.

clue.text: Thirty days in some islands — or just one

indicators.note: in means placed inside the letters for the islands

parts.note: CI stands for the Channel Islands
April has thirty days, abbreviated Apr

explanation.surface: A month spent in an island group, or on a single one.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are the British isles off the coast of Normandy; 'in' sets the month's short form inside their abbreviation, so 'some islands' gives way to just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is a single island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Rocket man turned up in city

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the V1 was a German wartime flying bomb, written VI
a valet is a manservant

explanation.surface: An astronaut appears in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses VI + VALET as one block.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is Israel's second-largest city, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Usual supporter for this was ancient

explanation.definitionFit: Standard means normal or typical; and a flag's bearer was once called its ancient, an old word for ensign.

clue.text: Result only possible after a case of Scotch

definitions.text: Result only possible after a case of Scotch

parts.words: Result only possible after a case of Scotch
parts.note: a 'case of Scotch' reads like a crate of whisky but means a trial in Scotland, whose courts have a third verdict between guilty and acquitted

explanation.walkthrough: Scottish courts uniquely allow a verdict short of acquittal when guilt is not established; 'case' is a law case, not a box of bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish third verdict, given when evidence falls short, is the outcome reached only in a Scots trial.

clue.text: President leading a dance .

parts.note: James K. Polk was the eleventh US president
taken as written

explanation.surface: A head of state leads off the dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to the next as one sentence. 'leading' just sets POLK before A.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively Bohemian couple dance in two-four time.

clue.text: with some American girl

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used, a run taken from inside it

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the president dances with a woman from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from the dance clue. 'some' takes a run of letters from inside AMERICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's given name, so a girl's name fits.

clue.text: Had life saved, perhaps, floundering in deep river

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone struggling in a deep river was rescued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floundering' rearranges the letters of DEEP and RIVER together. 'perhaps' warns that the definition is an example: a condemned man spared execution.
explanation.definitionFit: A condemned prisoner given a stay of execution has his life spared, which is what being granted clemency means.

clue.text: Portrayal of Madame Butterfly

explanation.definitionFit: A woman shown in a picture is literally a lady put on canvas; the painted lady is also an orange-and-black butterfly.

clue.text: After death I'm upset and tremble, note

parts.note: demise is a formal word for death

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these two letters are turned about

parts.note: to quaver is to shake or tremble, especially of a voice

explanation.surface: Someone is shaken and trembling after a bereavement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets what follows behind the synonym for death, and 'upset' turns I'M round to MI, the third note of the sol-fa scale by coincidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A demisemiquaver is a musical note, the thirty-second note, a quarter of a quaver.

clue.text: Multinational operation put forward unanimously

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, a multinational body
to pose a question is to put it forward

explanation.surface: An international mission is backed by everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Elected without opposition means with no dissenting voice, all in agreement.

clue.text: Top honour officer 'ad secured? Could be

annotationWithheld.why: Top honour officer 'ad secured? Could be (8): ACCOLADE is CO + LAD inside ACE, but the clue as held and on the scan has 'ad, not lad, and no word gives L
annotationWithheld.clue: Top honour officer 'ad secured? Could be

clue.text: Legal exercise

explanation.definitionFit: Lawful under a country's founding charter, and also the old term for a healthy daily walk.

clue.text: Danger to shipping in Channel is annoying

explanation.definitionFit: The Needles are chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight in the English Channel; to needle is to irritate.

clue.text: Spear once more cut fool's head

indicators.note: head means placed at the front, so the fool starts the word

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: cut means the word is clipped of its final letter

parts.note: again is another way of saying once more

explanation.surface: A spear is repaired once more after a fool's head is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mending a broken weapon, but 'cut' only clips the final letter of the synonym for 'once more', and 'head' sends the fool to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An assagai is a slender throwing spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Problem for person running part of Jersey

explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side from exertion; a jersey is a knitted pullover, made of loops of wool.

clue.text: Ecstatic on account of girl meeting boy

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
Joy is a woman's name
Ed is a short form of Edward, a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled because a girl has met a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Both girl and boy are names, a common crossword shortcut.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrilled to bits is being in a state of ecstasy.

clue.text: Happiness church can give author

parts.note: joy is happiness
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Joy and the church can inspire a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: James Joyce was the Irish author of Ulysses.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce was an Irish novelist and writer.

clue.text: Certain I've gone? It's only an assumption

indicators.note: gone says the letters of I've have departed from the longer word

parts.note: positive means sure or certain
the letters of I've, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone sure they have left is told it is only a supposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes IVE (from 'I've') from POSITIVE, a synonym of 'Certain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A posit is something postulated, a premise put forward as true.

clue.text: Way bowler uses to get England opener caught by colleague

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so the colleague's word goes round the letter

parts.note: an ally is a partner or colleague

indicators.note: opener means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler tries to get England's opening batsman caught by a teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface misleads: the bowler is a ten-pin bowler, whose lane is a bowling alley. 'caught by' puts E inside ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowling alley is the lane a ten-pin player sends the ball down.

clue.text: Put up what's seen as help for marksman

parts.note: to rear is to raise or put up
a sight is something seen

explanation.surface: A marksman's aid is described as something raised into view.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear sight is the aiming device near a gun's breech, lined up with the foresight.

clue.text: A single trip

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a single scores one run; and a run is a short journey, as in a run to the shops.

clue.text: Sculptor and authoress on record

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the writer's name sits against the record

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
Gertrude Stein was an American writer

explanation.surface: A sculptor and a woman writer appear on a disc.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Epstein was a British-American sculptor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was a celebrated twentieth-century sculptor.

clue.text: Why, it's said, I would ruin language

indicators.note: it's said means we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: the word why is pronounced like the letter Y
I'd is the contraction of I would
to dish someone's hopes is to ruin them

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why they would wreck a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' makes 'Why' the letter Y by sound. 'Dish' meaning ruin is British, as in dishing one's chances.
explanation.definitionFit: Yiddish is the Germanic tongue of Ashkenazi Jews, written in Hebrew script.
